headline: Sykes, ranked 81, takes on Van Gerwen for £60,000 tonight
standfirst: Tom Sykes meets Michael van Gerwen at 7:20pm, with Gian van Veen against Nathan Aspinall at 8:45pm, for places in Sunday's Grand Slam semi-finals.
body: The Grand Slam of Darts quarter-finals reach their last two ties tonight, and the first has the more intriguing shape. Tom Sykes, ranked 81st in the world, plays Michael van Gerwen, who is ranked 11th, at 7:20pm, a day after beating Luke Humphries 10-9 in the last 16. The winner of the first-to-16 match is guaranteed £60,000, and the loser takes home £35,000.

Van Gerwen has the pedigree: he won this event in 2017 and has beaten Sykes in the only meeting between them on record. His 12-month average of 96.22 is more than two points higher than Sykes's 93.88, and he has won 93 of 148 matches in that time with four titles to Sykes's none. But Sykes is making his first appearance at the event on record, and he has already beaten Luke Humphries this week.

The second tie, at 8:45pm, pairs Gian van Veen, the world No 3, with Nathan Aspinall, ranked 12th. Van Veen leads their head to head 5-3 across eight meetings, and has won 98 of 162 matches over the last year, yet no title. Aspinall averages 96.58 over the same period against Van Veen's 95.28 and has won one title.

Both men are chasing a first semi-final here. Van Veen's previous best at the event is a quarter-final in 2024, and Aspinall's is a quarter-final in 2020. Aspinall comes in off a 10-7 win over Gabriel Clemens, Van Veen off a 10-7 win over Martin Schindler.
Pick of the two is Sykes v Van Gerwen. The numbers favour the Dutchman, but a first-to-16 format leaves the underdog more time to recover from a slow start than a short match would.
